thesis: Clean industrial-gases compounder priced like the compounding already happened. Every engine gate passes — zero pledge, Z'' 6.94, no earnings-quality vetoes, 34% OPM, 9 facilities across East/South/Central India, and a Rs 481cr BHEL order (1.4x FY26 revenue) that validates its large-ASU engineering credentials. But at Rs 361 the market pays 42x earnings and 10x the engine's Rs 35 DCF fair value; the Sep-2026 pop on the BHEL news (+5%) shows sentiment is chasing, not value. Quality is not the question — price is. There is no entry until the price comes to the business, not the other way round.
risks: Valuation extreme: 42.2x TTM earnings, 5.2x book; price Rs 361 is 10.2x the engine's Rs 35.29 DCF fair value — the entire upside case is priced in and then some
Earnings-quality flags: TTM other income Rs 60.3cr (~40% of PBT); FY25 CFO was Rs 4cr vs PAT Rs 83cr (working-capital drag) — E2 passed only on non-persistence

BHEL mega-order is build-and-transfer EPC at ~5% EBITDA margin (JM Financial est.) — 1.4x FY26 revenue concentrated in one low-margin turnkey project; execution slippage hits both revenue and reputation
Customer concentration: steel 35% of sales, oxygen 50% of gas mix; merchant gases are cyclical with steel
Post-IPO volatility: listed Jun-2025 at ~Rs 486 (issue Rs 400), fell to Rs 175 low, now Rs 361 — 16 months of price history, thin institutional float (11.6%)
Model caveat: bare-schema DCF uses a 15% FCFF margin fallback vs 34% reported OPM, so Rs 35.29 is conservative — but even 3x that FV leaves no margin of safety at Rs 361
